messages:
emily: Heads up, deploy-bot blocked the prod rollout for 3.8.0 during pre-cut compliance checks. SBOM license mismatch + one medium vuln on a transitive dep. Need quick decision: pin transitive dep, hotpatch, or rollback to 3.7.5.

raj: what does the license mismatch look like? can we ship with an exception?

jess: paste from deploy-bot below. license is 'GPL-2.0-only' detected in `third_party/png-helpers` (transitive). Our policy blocks GPL-only libs unless dual-licensed or vendor-approved.

deploy-bot: compliance: sbom-license-check/4681119900 FAILED
- package: third_party/png-helpers@1.2.0
- license: GPL-2.0-only (policy: block)
vuln-scan-staging/4681119901: 1 medium (zlib-ng 2.0.4) - CVE-2021-2222 - score 5.6 - exploitability moderate
artifact: gcr.io/redwood/release/3.8.0-canary@sha256:ef01cdef

tom: from an engineering POV, png-helpers is only used by a small image-conversion path behind opt-in customers. we can vendor patch or swap implementation, but that takes ~2 days. pinning won't change license.

emily: options: (1) roll back to 3.7.5 now, (2) grant temporary release exception (legal sign-off required), or (3) block and hotpatch (delays release). change window is tight. legal oncall is reachable?

raj: pinging @legal-oncall. we should also consider scoped rollout: allow EU canary only? license is global, though.

infra-bot: cosign: attestation present for artifact ef01cdef, signature verified. SBOM signed: https://artifacts.internal/sbom/3.8.0/cosign.sig (sha256:aa55bb66cc77dd88ee99ff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff0011223344)

jess: surprising that attestation exists given sbom license fail - CI signs SBOM before policy checks. evidence is there but we still need compliance decision.

legal-oncall (via raj): we can approve a short-lived release exception if product owners accept mitigation and track remediation in SEC ticket. need rationale + scope + rollback owner + deadline.

emily: proposed mitigation note: "png-helpers GPL-2.0-only used only in opt-in image-conversion. Customers using default flow unaffected; we will remove dependency in 3.8.1 within 14 days. Exception requested to allow EU canary only."

tom: agree with note. also propose runtime guard: disable image-conversion by default and route traffic to legacy path for the canary. fast toggle.

raj: who's the rollback owner if something goes wrong?

jess: i'm available to run `releases/rollback-quick` if canary shows problems. takes ~8m to revert and redeploy 3.7.5.

legal-oncall: approve conditional exception for canary rollout in US-west and EU regions (50% traffic) provided:
- mitigation note in release docs
- SEC ticket created: SEC-6001
- remediation ETA 14 days
- rollback owner assigned

emily: ✅ created SEC-6001: https://triage.internal/sec/6001
mitigation note pushed to release notes. runtime flag added: `feature.image_conversion=false` for canary.

deploy-bot: action: canary rollout -> US-west & EU (50% traffic), start_ts 4681123600. Attestation linked.

jess: monitoring hooks added, alert on error-rate >= 1% or CPU spike. PagerDuty watch set for releases-oncall.

emily: decision: proceed with scoped canary under exception. global rollout blocked until remediation or full legal approval. if alerts trip, rollback to 3.7.5 (jess owner). timebox: 3 hours of canary monitoring.

tom: noted. I'll work on the removal plan for 3.8.1 and post updates to SEC-6001.

emily: thanks team. closing thread for now — will reopen if rollback occurs. :white_check_mark:
